citations.narrative:
The inspector observed the following inaccuracies in the facility's inventory and acquisition records:
** White-Tailed deer: The record did not include two offspring born a few weeks prior to the inspection.
** Domestic Pigeon: The record did not include one juvenile pigeon hatched about three weeks prior to the inspection.
** Fallow deer: The inventory lists 9 animals. The inspector and licensee counted 10 animals at the time of inspection.
The licensee reported this was a calculation error when updating records.
** Muscovy ducks: The inventory lists 5 muscovy ducks. The inspector and licensee counted 4 muscovy ducks at the time
of inspection. Acquisition records were not available to review. The licensee was unsure why this number was inaccurate.
Accurate and well-maintained records of acquisition and disposition of animals is critical to identify and trace animals and
to make sure all animals are accounted for.
Every exhibitor shall make, keep, and maintain records or forms which fully and correctly disclose the following
information regarding animals purchased or otherwise acquired, owned, held, leased, or otherwise in his or her
possession or under his or her control, or which is transported, sold, euthanized, or otherwise disposed of by that dealer
or exhibitor. The records shall include any offspring born or hatched of any animal while in his or her possession or under
his or her control, to the extent that any identification or counting of offspring can be carried out without unduly disturbing
nesting or rearing activities.

The water quality in an aquatic area available to 4 muscovy ducks is inadequately managed.
There are two available aquatic areas in an outdoor enclosure housing 4 muscovy ducks and several other non-aquatic
species of birds. The inspector observed one rectangular aquatic area that contained shallow, opaque, deep green water
with some fallen tree debris in the water. There was a second aquatic area to the left that contained deeper water, which
appeared to have adequate water quality and depth. Neither aquatic areas utilized an aeration system.
Pools or other aquatic areas without drainage systems must be aerated and have an incoming flow of fresh water or be
managed in a manner that maintains appropriate water quality in accordance with current professionally accepted
standards appropriate for the species.
Correction date: September 19, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
